record.paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
record.context_brief: Oblivious routing C plus D objective
record.original_question: In oblivious routing, let C be congestion and D be the maximum path length produced by the routing. Which classes of networks admit oblivious routing algorithms for which C + D is close to the offline optimum, so that packet delivery can be scheduled in time proportional to C + D?

evidence.quote: Another interesting open problem is to find classes of networks in which oblivious routing gives C + D close to the off-line optimal, where C is the congestion and D is the maximum path length.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider packet routing in an undirected network $G=(V,E)$. A routing instance consists of a multiset of source-destination pairs $\{(s_i,t_i)\}_{i=1}^k$, one packet per pair. A routing scheme assigns to each pair $(s_i,t_i)$ a path $P_i$ from $s_i$ to $t_i$ in $G$. Given such an assignment, define
- the congestion $C = \max_{e \in E} |\{ i : e \in P_i \}|$,
- the dilation $D = \max_i |P_i|$ (the maximum hop-length of any chosen path).

It is known that, given the paths, the packets can then be scheduled and delivered in time $O(C+D)$. A routing scheme is called oblivious if the path $P_i$ chosen for the pair $(s_i,t_i)$ depends only on $(s_i,t_i)$ (and possibly private randomness) and not on the other source-destination pairs in the instance.

The offline optimum for an instance is $\mathrm{OPT}(G,\{(s_i,t_i)\}) = \min (C^* + D^*)$, where the minimum is over all path assignments and $C^*, D^*$ are the corresponding congestion and dilation.

Problem. Characterize, or exhibit, classes of networks $G$ that admit an oblivious routing algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ such that for every routing instance the resulting congestion $C$ and dilation $D$ satisfy
$$ C + D \;\le\; f(|V|) \cdot \mathrm{OPT}(G,\{(s_i,t_i)\}) $$
for some small (e.g. polylogarithmic) factor $f$, so that packets can be delivered in time proportional to $C+D$ that is close to the offline optimum.
artifact.status_search_result: Ghaffari, Haeupler, and Zuzic (STOC 2021, "Hop-Constrained Oblivious Routing") proved that every undirected network admits an oblivious routing scheme whose (congestion + dilation) is within a poly(log n) factor of the offline optimum, resolving this question affirmatively for general undirected graphs. Earlier work had given matching results for specific classes (e.g. d-dimensional meshes within an O(d^2) factor). Subsequent work (Haeupler–Hershkowitz–Zuzic STOC 2022; electrical-flow based schemes, ITCS 2024) refines the bounds and gives efficient constructions.

status_evidence.title: Hop-Constrained Oblivious Routing (Ghaffari, Haeupler, Zuzic)
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the existence of an oblivious routing scheme that is poly(log n)-competitive in terms of (congestion + dilation), thus resolving a well-known question in oblivious routing.
status_evidence.claim: General undirected graphs admit oblivious routing schemes with C+D within a poly(log n) factor of optimum.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Oblivious Path Selection on the Mesh (Busch, Magdon-Ismail)
status_evidence.snippet: For d-dimensional meshes, an oblivious algorithm achieves congestion and dilation each within O(d^2) of optimal, hence C+D within O(d^2) of optimal.
status_evidence.claim: Meshes are an explicit class with near-optimal oblivious C+D.

status_evidence.title: Electrical Flows for Polylogarithmic Competitive Oblivious Routing (ITCS 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Polylogarithmic competitive oblivious routing for the congestion+dilation objective via electrical flows.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work refines and simplifies the polylog-competitive construction.
